s: Muscat geosite where river gravels on the ophiolite are capped by Eocene lagoon limestone
dr: Al-Khod Formation Campanian(?)–Maastrichtian(?); Seeb Formation basal Lutetian
el: Seeb Formation basal unit about 20–40 m thick
te: Where rivers ran over an ocean floor
ta: حيث جرت الأنهار فوق قاع محيط قديم
se: At Al Khoud, gravels left by ancient rivers lie on top of old ocean floor rock, and a warm lagoon later laid limestone over them
sa: في الخوض ترقد حصى أنهار قديمة فوق صخور كانت يومًا قاعًا للمحيط، ثم غطّتها لاحقًا حجارة جيرية ترسّبت في بحيرة ساحلية دافئة
desc: Al Khoud in Wilayat As Seeb is one of the 30 Muscat geosites in the Ministry of Tourism's Muscat Geoheritage guide launched in 2012. Here the siliciclastic Al-Khod Formation, of Campanian(?) to Maastrichtian(?) age, was deposited nonconformably on the Semail Ophiolite. Above an angular unconformity, shallow-marine limestones of Paleocene to Miocene age follow, including the Seeb Formation, whose basal unit is about 20–40 m of lagoonal packstones and grainstones dated by foraminifera to the middle Eocene. Dinosaur footprints, bones and fossil dung about 70 million years old have been reported from the Al Khoudh area by Sultan Qaboos University geologists and the Oman Geological Society.
sig: A compact record of the land surface that formed on the Semail Ophiolite after its emplacement and of the return of the sea.
ex: Mattern et al. (2023); Muscat Geoheritage guide (2012)
disc: Al-Khod Formation rests on the ophiolite
refs: Mattern, F., Scharf, A., Al-Sayigh, A.R., Al-Wahaibi, N., Galluccio, L., Frijia, G. & Al-Salmani, M. (2023). Lagoonal Microfacies, Lithostratigraphy, Correlation and Shale Migration of the Basal Middle Eocene Seeb Formation (Rusayl Embayment, Sultanate of Oman). Geosciences 13, 254. https://doi.org/10.3390/geosciences13090254
eTurboNews (27 June 2012). Omani tourism launches Muscat Geoheritage auto guide. https://eturbonews.com/omani-tourism-launches-muscat-geoheritage-auto-guide/
Oman Observer (18 September 2023). Al Khoudh was home to dinosaurs 70 million years ago. https://www.omanobserver.om/ampArticle/1143045
conf: The guide's exact geosite point is not published; coordinates are Mattern et al. (2023) Section 2 on the road into Al-Khod village (23°34′23.79″N 58°07′42.04″E). Timeline start/end are broad estimates for the Campanian and the end of the Lutetian. Dinosaur findings come from a newspaper report. Arabic name is a descriptive rendering.

s: Dark-sky reserve on the Jabal Shams highlands, one of the first in the Middle East
te: A roof of stars over Oman's highest mountain
ta: سقف من النجوم فوق أعلى جبال عُمان
se: High on Jabal Shams, Oman protects the night itself, keeping the sky dark so families can see the stars
sa: على قمم جبل شمس تحمي عُمان الليل نفسه، فتُبقي السماء مظلمة ليرى الناس النجوم بوضوح
desc: The Western Hajar Starlight Reserve in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate was established by Royal Decree 40/2019 of 8 May 2019, its boundary defined by 12 points in the decree annex. The Al Hajar Geopark booklet gives its area as 386 km², at 1,300–3,000 m with most terrain above 2,000 m. It contains Jabal Shams, the highest peak in eastern Arabia, and the gorge known as the Grand Canyon of Oman, and its fossil-rich layers record former shallow seas. The reserve was created to promote stargazing and limit light pollution, and it also holds the largest number of endangered juniper trees.
sig: Described as one of the first starlight reserves in the Middle East, protecting dark skies over Oman's highest mountains.
ex: Royal Decree 40/2019; Al Hajar Geopark booklet
refs: Royal Decree 40/2019 Establishing the Western Hajar Starlight Reserve in the Governorate of Al-Dakhiliyah (English translation, FAOLEX). https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/oma205970E.pdf

s: Lagoon at the mouth of Wadi Sayq in far western Dhofar, protected for nature and archaeology
te: The hidden lagoon of western Dhofar
se: Reached only by a long wadi or by sea, Khor Kharfot hides a lagoon, springs and green monsoon forests beside ancient ruins
sa: لا يُبلغ خور خرفوت إلا عبر وادٍ طويل أو من البحر، وفيه بحيرة وينابيع وغابات يكسوها الخريف بالخضرة إلى جانب أطلال قديمة
desc: Khor Kharfot lies on the Arabian Sea coast between Rakhyut and Dhalkut in Dhofar, at the mouth of Wadi Sayq, about 100 km west of Salalah. Royal Decree 58/2021 of 23 August 2021 made it an archaeological reserve of 143.4 km² with mountains, woodlands, wadis and coast watered by the annual Khareef monsoon. A large permanent brackish lagoon with about 1 m of organic mud sits behind a sand barrier about 4 m high, within late Holocene deposits. Surface remains assessed in 1993 suggested habitation phases from the Neolithic to the late Islamic period, and the khor is believed to have been an ancient frankincense port.
sig: A rare intact monsoon coastal valley where natural habitats and a long archaeological record are protected together.
refs: Abbasi, I.A. (2016). Geological assessment of the Khor Kharfot sediments, western Dhofar region, Sultanate of Oman. Sultan Qaboos University Journal for Science 21(1), 16–25. https://archive.dev-bookofmormoncentral.org/sites/default/files/archive-files/pdf/abbasi/2016-07-29/iftikhar_a._abbasi_geological_assessment_of_the_khor_kharfot_sediments_2016.pdf
Royal Decree 58/2021 establishing Khor Kharfot Archaeological Reserve in Dhofar Governorate. https://qanoon.om/p/2021/rd2021058/

conf: Coordinates as published by Abbasi (2016): 16°43′51″N 53°20′E (longitude to the minute). The 1993 habitation phases (P. Costa) are cited via Aston (2016), not the original report. Layer could also be archaeological.

s: Islands, reefs and fjord coasts of Musandam protected as a national park
se: Musandam's national park joins nine islands, coral reefs and quiet bays where dolphins swim and thousands of seabirds nest
sa: يضمّ المنتزه الوطني في مسندم تسع جزر وشعابًا مرجانية وخلجانًا هادئة تسبح فيها الدلافين وتعشّش فيها آلاف الطيور البحرية
desc: The Natural National Park in Musandam Governorate was established by Royal Decree 54/2022 of 28 June 2022, with boundaries set by an annex of more than 400 points. The Environment Authority gives a total area of 1,149.40 km², including nine offshore islands of limestone and ancient coral reef with steep cliffs, plus shallow coasts, shoals and bays. Surveys recorded coral reefs, bottlenose, common and spinner dolphins, humpback whales, sea snakes and nesting green turtles. More than 200 plant species were found in a preliminary survey, and seabirds number in the thousands, notably on Umm Al Tair island.
sig: The largest protected area in Musandam, covering the marine and island landscapes at the entrance to the Arabian Gulf.
refs: Royal Decree 54/2022 establishing the Natural National Park in Musandam Governorate. https://qanoon.om/p/2022/rd2022054/
Oman Observer (2022). Royal Decree embodies Musandam's geographical and environmental diversity: EA. https://www.omanobserver.om/ampArticle/1121511
conf: Coordinates are the centre of the bounds of the decree's main annex polygon, read as UTM zone 40N (WGS 84; annex lists northing before easting). 'Largest protected area in Musandam' is inferred from the area figure. The existing app entry khor-ash-sham lies within the park area but is a separate feature.

s: Mountain reserve above Al Rustaq for the Arabian ibex and other wild mammals
se: In the mountains of South Al Batinah, the Arabian ibex, foxes and lynx roam valleys lined with dense trees
sa: في جبال جنوب الباطنة يجوب الوعل العربي والثعالب والوشق وديانًا تحفّها الأشجار الكثيفة
desc: Al Rustaq Wildlife Reserve in South Al Batinah Governorate was established by Royal Decree 41/2019 of 8 May 2019, published in Official Gazette 1292, with a 23-point boundary annex. It covers 254 km² of mountains, valleys, water bodies and dense trees along wadi banks. Six wild mammal species are reported, including the endangered Arabian ibex, mountain fox, lynx, white-tailed mongoose and hedgehog, along with 15 bird species including eagles and ospreys. The Directorate of Environment in South Al Batinah monitors the reserve.
sig: Protects a mountain refuge for the Arabian ibex in the western Hajar range.
refs: Royal Decree 41/2019 establishing the Al Rustaq Wildlife Reserve in South Al Batinah Governorate. https://qanoon.om/p/2019/rd2019041/
Oman Observer (2024). Al Rustaq Wildlife Reserve a magnet for adventure tourism lovers. https://www.omanobserver.om/ampArticle/1153587
conf: Coordinates are the centroid of the decree's annex polygon, read as UTM zone 40N (WGS 84); the computed area (254 km²) matches the published figure.

s: Limestone mountain reserve in South Ash Sharqiyah centred on the Arabian tahr
te: The mountain of the Arabian tahr
se: On the steep slopes of Jabal Qahwan lives the shy Arabian tahr, alongside wolves, foxes and caracals
sa: على المنحدرات الشديدة لجبل قهوان يعيش الطهر العربي الخجول، ومعه الذئاب والثعالب والوشق
desc: Jabal Qahwan Nature Reserve in South Ash Sharqiyah Governorate was established by Royal Decree 50/2014 of 21 September 2014, published in Official Gazette 1072, with a 43-point boundary annex. It is a sedimentary mountain range rising to 1,000–1,300 m, with steep slopes, gravel wadis, caves, fossils and plains. The Arabian tahr is its key species, with gazelles, Arabian wolf, red and mountain foxes, caracal, mongooses and wildcat, and resident birds include the Egyptian vulture and two falcon species. Ancient graves and limestone rock carvings dated to the third millennium BC lie within it.
sig: One of Oman's protected strongholds for the endangered Arabian tahr, combining wildlife and rock art heritage.
disc: Arabian tahr is the key species
Rock carvings of the third millennium BC
refs: Royal Decree 50/2014 establishing Jabal Qahwan Nature Reserve in South Al Sharqiyah Governorate. https://qanoon.om/p/2014/rd2014050/
Oman Daily (2023). محمية جبل قهوان الطبيعية. https://www.omandaily.om/article/1130259
conf: Coordinates are the centroid of the decree's annex polygon, read as UTM zone 40N (WGS 84). That polygon computes to about 290 km²; Oman Daily prints 28,905 km², apparently a misplaced decimal, so no area is given. A WDPA-derived listing placing it in North Ash Sharqiyah (23.15, 58.6) conflicts with the decree and was not used. Oman Daily article year not confirmed.

s: Artificial wetland fed by treated water, a Ramsar site with 305 bird species
te: A bird oasis made from clean water
se: Next to Muscat, treated water fills a chain of ponds where more than 300 kinds of birds stop to rest and feed
sa: قرب مسقط تملأ المياه المعالجة سلسلة من البرك تتوقف فيها أكثر من 300 نوع من الطيور للراحة والتغذية
desc: Al Ansab Wetland in Bawshar is an artificial wetland about 15 km from the centre of Muscat, managed by Haya Water. Treated water from an associated treatment facility feeds a set of ponds that create habitat in an otherwise arid setting. It was designated Ramsar Site no. 2406 on 22 March 2020 and covers 54 ha. It supports 305 recorded resident and migratory bird species, including the endangered Egyptian vulture and steppe eagle and the vulnerable common pochard and sooty falcon.
sig: A Ramsar wetland showing how reused water can create valuable urban bird habitat in an arid capital.
refs: Ramsar Sites Information Service. Annotated summary of Ramsar Sites: Oman (Al Ansab Wetland, site no. 2406). https://rsis.ramsar.org/sites/default/files/rsiswp_search/exports/Ramsar-Sites-annotated-summary-Oman.pdf

s: Underground falaj at Birkat Al Mouz, part of the Aflaj World Heritage site
dr: UNESCO World Heritage 2006, Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman
te: The hidden river of Birkat Al Mouz
se: Under the ground at Birkat Al Mouz a channel carries mountain water to palm gardens, guarded by watchtowers
sa: تحت أرض بركة الموز تجري قناة تحمل مياه الجبل إلى بساتين النخيل، وتحرسها أبراج المراقبة
desc: Falaj Al-Khatmeen at Birkat Al Mouz, Wilayat of Nizwa, is one of the five aflaj inscribed in 2006 as the Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman, representing some 3,000 aflaj still working in the country. It is a daoudi (underground) falaj fed from Wadi Al Meaidin, running about 2.4 km from its mother well to the shari'a, mostly underground, and serving a demand area of about 723,124 m². Two watchtowers and a mosque stand in the demand area, and Bait Al-Redadah Fort sits over the channel. UNESCO notes it as one of the most intact components, with water used for both civic and agricultural purposes. The component covers 135.028 ha with a 1,756.4 ha buffer zone.
sig: One of the most intact of Oman's World Heritage aflaj, still sharing water by time as it has for centuries.

s: Long underground falaj of Izki with 17 branches, part of the Aflaj World Heritage site
dr: UNESCO World Heritage 2006, Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman
se: In Izki one underground falaj splits into seventeen branches to water the gardens of two old quarters
sa: في إزكي يتفرّع فلج واحد تحت الأرض إلى سبعة عشر فرعًا ليسقي بساتين حارتين قديمتين
desc: Falaj Al-Malki in the Wilayat of Izki, Ad Dakhiliyah, is one of the five aflaj inscribed in 2006 as the Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman. It is a daoudi (underground) falaj about 14.8 km long including 17 branches, which serve the Nazar and Al-Yaman quarters and a demand area of about 1,572,730 m². A watchtower stands on a hill above the plantations, with remains of two others and a few traditional houses. UNESCO notes building types found at no other component, and the component covers 600 ha with a 4,255.71 ha buffer zone.
sig: The longest of the five World Heritage aflaj, a working millennia-old water landscape.

s: Rustaq falaj with a 50 m deep mother well, sundial and water-auction building
dr: UNESCO World Heritage 2006, Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman
el: Mother well 50 m deep; about 5.8 km with branches
se: In Al Rustaq farmers once used a sundial to share the water of a falaj that begins in a well 50 m deep
sa: في الرستاق كان المزارعون يتقاسمون مياه فلج يبدأ من بئر عمقها 50 مترًا مستعينين بمزولة شمسية
desc: Falaj Al-Muyassar in the Wilayat of Al Rustaq, South Al Batinah, is one of the five aflaj inscribed in 2006 as the Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman. It is a daoudi (underground) falaj that starts from a mother well 50 m deep and runs about 5.8 km including branches, serving a demand area of about 1,133,698 m². A watchtower stands beside the shari'a, with abandoned mud-brick houses, a sundial and a water-auction building. UNESCO notes its highly authentic agricultural areas and the best-preserved traditional management practices, and the component covers 300.501 ha.
sig: Keeps the best-preserved traditional water management of the World Heritage aflaj.

s: Spring-fed mountain falaj of Wilayat Sur, part of the Aflaj World Heritage site
dr: UNESCO World Heritage 2006, Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman
el: About 1.6 km open channel and aqueduct
te: The spring channel high in the mountains
se: High above a mountain village near Sur, spring water flows along an open channel and a small aqueduct to the fields
sa: فوق قرية جبلية قرب صور تنساب مياه نبع في قناة مكشوفة وقناطر صغيرة حتى تبلغ الحقول
desc: Falaj Al-Jeela at Al-Jeela village in Wilayat Sur, South Ash Sharqiyah, is the only one of the five World Heritage aflaj in the Sharqi range, the others clustering around Al Jabal Al Akhdar. It is an aini (spring-fed) falaj drawing on a spring high above the village, carried by about 1.6 km of open channel and a small aqueduct to a collection tank, serving a demand area of about 14,000 m². A small mosque and traditional houses belong to the system, and its flow is stable. UNESCO describes it as an excellent, still-functioning traditional falaj landscape, among the most intact; the component covers 30.952 ha with a 3,839.46 ha buffer zone.
sig: The spring-fed example of Oman's World Heritage aflaj, still the main water source of its village.
disc: Only component in the Sharqi range
